10.1002_aenm.202504110: In this study, 3d transition metal chlorides are evaluated exhibiting high Li diffusivity, as determined by high‐throughput computational screening, and create a redox electron orbital energy‐level diagram to explain their working potentials and reversibility‐decreasing Cl‐release behavior. The redox‐level diagram enables the design of high‐potential chloride electrode materials that suppress Cl release by adjusting the transition metal environment of the redox center. Li 2 FeCl 4 , containing elementally strategically ideal Fe, exhibits a high energy density of 330 Wh (kg‐cathode) −1 via redox‐level‐tuning partial O coordination (Li 2.2 FeCl 3.8 O 0.2 ). This energy density is the highest recorded value for Fe‐based solid‐state batteries offering high safety and high charge/discharge rates. First‐principles calculations confirm and correlate this high energy density to Fe redox‐level tuning and capacity development up to the Cl‐release potential. This redox‐level tuning approach can be extended to other electrode material systems, including oxides, sulfides, and halides, to develop high‐energy‐density batteries.
10.1002_aenm.71544: Reducing iridium (Ir) loading while maintaining high activity and durability remains a critical challenge for proton exchange membrane water electrolysis. While oxide‐supported catalysts offer a pathway for Ir reduction, their intrinsic low electronic conductivity and inefficient charge transfer at catalyst‐support interfaces remain imperative bottlenecks. Herein, we report a synergistic interfacial engineering strategy of catalyst‐support based on partial ex‐solution of Bi from a Bi 3 TaO 7 support. Ex‐solved Bi forms highly active Ir─Bi alloy domains while generating a Bi‐deficient support and markedly improving the conductivity of the support. Moreover, this coupled reconstruction lowers the work function of the Ir‐based catalyst while increasing the work function of the support, shifting the catalyst‐support contact from rectifying to ohmic, thereby facilitating efficient electron transport. The resulting IrBi/Bi 3‐x TaO 7 exhibits enhanced half‐cell oxygen evolution reaction activity (248 mV at 10 mA/cm 2 ), mass activity (1077 mA/mg Ir at 1.55 V), and durability (15.8 h). Furthermore, single‐cell measurements achieve outstanding performance of 1.824 V at 2 A/cm 2 with a low Ir loading of 0.38 mg/cm 2 and negligible voltage degradation over 100 h. This work highlights a generalizable strategy for simultaneous electronic integration of catalyst and support, offering new insights into the design of efficient and durable electrocatalysts for PEMWE.
10.1002_ps.71447: BACKGROUND Multiple stressors have been identified as threats to pollinators, many of which are related to human activities. Pesticides are among the most studied stressors affecting pollinators, whereas microplastic residues represent an emerging and less studied threat. This study investigated the combined effects of polystyrene microplastics and the pesticide flupyradifurone on three pollinator species: Apis mellifera ligustica , Bombus terrestris , and Eristalis tenax . Acute oral toxicity tests were conducted by feeding individuals with different doses of flupyradifurone alone or in combination with a fixed concentration of microplastics. RESULTS The median lethal dose (LD 50 ) of flupyradifurone differed among species. In A. mellifera , the LD 50 was 0.91 μg/insect (95% confidence interval (CI): 0.38–1.20). In B. terrestris , the LD 50 decreased from 46.10 μg/insect (95% CI: 37.55–59.02) to 31.17 μg/insect (95% CI: 25.66–38.11) in the presence of microplastics, showing a different response under co‐exposure. For E. tenax , a reliable LD 50 could not be estimated. Only the highest tested dose (4.8 μg/insect) caused significantly higher mortality than the control, with no effect of microplastics. CONCLUSION Acute mortality was mainly related to flupyradifurone exposure, while the effect of polystyrene microplastics differed among species. In B. terrestris , the presence of microplastics was associated with a lower LD 50 , suggesting that interactions between microplastics and pesticides may differ among pollinator species. Longer‐term studies are needed to better understand the potential effects of microplastics on pollinators. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.
10.1002_smll.202507190: Aqueous zinc metal batteries suffer from uncontrollable dendrite growth and undesirable side reactions, which drastically compromise the battery performance and practical application. To address these issues, an accordion‐type multifunctional coating of Cu‐V 2 CBr 2 MXene with zincophilic and hydrophobic properties is developed by molten salt etching to achieve highly redox reversibile of zinc. Experimental results and theoretical calculations demonstrate that the ‐Br terminating groups have a strong electronegativity, which can electronically modify the surface of MXene, affecting the local electrochemical environment. This creates a low surface energy and a strongly hydrophobic surface, thereby inhibiting the side reactions. In addition, the in situ formation of copper nanoparticles within the interlayers provides abundant nucleation sites and promotes uniform electron distribution throughout the framework, thereby regulating Zn 2+ ions flux and facilitating uniform zinc deposition. As a result, the symmetric cells demonstrate good rate performance and stable cycling performance for up to 1700 h at 10 mA cm −2 . The full batteries paired with iodine‐loaded porous carbon cathode exhibit an excellent capacity retention of 89.3% after 5000 cycles at 5 C. This work opens a new pathway to modulate the zinc anode interface process, which can also be extended to other aqueous batteries.
10.1016_j.ceramint.2026.05.070: Corrosion presents a significant challenge in today’s urbanized world, severely affecting industries such as oil and gas, automotive, aerospace and construction, where material integrity and strength are crucial for long-term performance. Nickel-based coatings provide a cost-effective solution by enhancing mechanical and electrochemical properties. In this study, novel Ni-P/ZrB 2 nanocomposite coatings were developed with varying concentrations of ZrB 2 nanoparticles (0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1.00 g/L) on carbon steel by electrodeposition technique. The fabricated coatings were analyzed using various characterization techniques. In parallel, COMSOL simulation was studied to investigate the distribution of current density and Ni 2+ species in Ni-P coating. Additionally, predicted coating thickness values were obtained, ranging from 5-8 near the center and 10-15 at the edges. The structural (XRD, SEM), compositional (EDX, XPS) and topographical (AFM) analysis revealed an amorphous structure and support the incorporation of ZrB 2 into the Ni-P matrix. Ni-P/ 0.75 g/L ZrB 2 nanocomposite coatings exhibited the highest improvement in microhardness (34%), wear resistance (52%) and corrosion protection efficiency (92%) as compared to the Ni-P coating. This increase can be attributed to the (a) dispersion hardening effect due to ZrB 2 (b) load-bearing capability (c) reduction in active sites and filling of micropores in Ni-P matrix. Erosion analysis at different impact angles confirms the improvement in erosive wear resistance with the addition of ZrB 2 nanoparticles. An improvement in hydrogen permeation barrier is observed with increasing ZrB 2 concentration, 1.0 g/L reducing the hydrogen diffusion and penetration into the coating.
10.1016_j.enconman.2026.121873: Efficient thermal management of electric vehicle battery modules requires modeling approaches that capture spatial thermal gradients while remaining computationally efficient for system level evaluation under realistic driving conditions. This study presents a multi-scale electro-thermal-aging framework based on systematic three-dimensional (3D) to one-dimensional (1D) model reduction for a 360 cell immersion-cooled lithium-ion battery module integrated into a complete electric vehicle model. Convective heat transfer coefficients and pressure losses extracted from CFD simulations are implemented in a reduced 24-node thermal model representing coolant flow direction effects. Heat generation is obtained from an experimentally validated electrochemical model, and a temperature-dependent degradation model capturing solid-electrolyte interphase growth, cathode film formation, and active material isolation is coupled to each node to enable spatially resolved aging prediction. The reduced model reproduces 3D temperature distributions within 2 °C while decreasing computational time. Vehicle level simulations under NEDC and US06 driving cycles demonstrate that immersion cooling maintains high thermal uniformity, resulting in less than 0.5 % state of health variation across module nodes. The proposed framework provides a computationally efficient tool for evaluating immersion cooling architectures and quantifying their impact on thermal performance, degradation, and vehicle range under realistic driving scenarios.
10.1016_j.jece.2026.125105: Microplastics research increasingly relies on magnetic separation to recover engineered particles from experimental systems. However, current magnetic approaches generally require post-production surface modification with magnetic nanoparticles, increasing cost, complexity, and the risk of demagnetization and secondary pollution. Here, we demonstrate, using a commercially available spray paint containing iron-based pigments, that laboratory-generated paint microplastics can exhibit inherent magnetic responsiveness. Spray-paint microplastics (2.7–47.7 μm diameter) were generated without additional magnetic modification and recovered directly from water and soil using permanent magnets (99% in water and 97% in soil using a neodymium magnet). Their polymeric composition was confirmed by FTIR, while X-ray fluorescence identified iron as the dominant magnetic element responsible for their magnetic behavior. Notably, these recoveries were achieved using inexpensive permanent magnets generating fields below 0.1 T, substantially lower than the field strengths typically reported for magnetic microplastic separation, without requiring expensive supplies and infrastructure. This approach is expected to reduce the risk of magnetic material loss associated with surface-modified microplastics. However, the long-term stability of the magnetic properties over repeated recovery cycles remains to be experimentally verified. This proof-of-concept introduces a robust, inexpensive, and experimentally accessible platform for producing and recovering magnetic paint microplastics, providing a valuable tool for laboratory studies on ecotoxicology, weathering, transport, bioaccumulation, and environmental fate while reducing infrastructure requirements and expanding access to microplastics research in resource-limited laboratories.
